_comment: Canonical guard wiring (CER-1741). Declarative source of truth for WHICH
guard hooks are wired to WHICH tool matchers.
settings.json itself stays chezmoi-ignored because Claude Code rewrites it
in place; chezmoi must not fight that. This file holds only the guard
subset, and 50-claude-guard-wiring.sh splices it in with jq, leaving every
other key — permissions, model, env, non-guard hooks — untouched.
The splice is ADDITIVE and never removes an entry. Guards are the only
thing binding agents that run with --dangerously-skip-permissions, so a
wiring mechanism that can subtract is a mechanism that can silently disarm
a host. That is CER-1743, and it is not a mistake worth automating.
Matchers are per-tool and are NOT redundant: worktree-jail appears four
times because a PreToolUse entry binds one matcher, so Bash/Edit/Write/
NotebookEdit each need their own. Collapsing them removes jail enforcement
from three of four tool types.
_host_specific_note: audit-send-keys, moshi-hook, relay-poll) are deliberately NOT listed.
They are wired by hand on the hosts that need them, and because the
splice never removes anything, leaving them out here cannot unwire them.
